## 2. Learning metrics (analytics steward)

Report the controllable inputs and the outputs separately. Engagement numbers come last and come labelled.

**There is still no real-learner data.** Production exists (r4-r6 on system-3-company.vercel.app; r6 shipped 2026-10-15 01:07 UTC with 48 newly published lessons, 635 now published), and `/api/events` is live. But the route only does `console.log` (src/app/api/events/route.ts), nothing exports or keeps those logs, and company/ops/deployments/ holds only its README. Our own smoke tests are not learners either. So recall, completion and dwell are **empty, not zero**, and this record makes **no learning claim**. EXP-002 is still "designed, not run" with no session date, and its committed prediction (recall >= 60%; wrong if <= 45%) stands as written. The first number needs two things: events that persist (W-706, backend-engineer, open) and either a founder-approved deploy carrying that or an EXP-002 session. The earliest revisit-recall number is deploy day + 1 (`REVISIT_SCHEDULE_DAYS = [1, 3, 7, 21]`).

**Logging check, the 6 published lessons whose QA record says fail.** two-said-blue, below-critical-mass, bid-what-its-worth, mild-preferences-sharp-divides, prices-sort-the-buyers and contact-order-matters all shipped as published in r6. Each one's only per-lesson record, `company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-14-qa.md` (commit 68e4fde, 10:19 UTC), says `result: **fail**` on the 24 px tap-target check. The publish gate in tools/company.mjs (`launchGates`) checks that a QA record exists, not what it says, so this passed `check`. Before calling these defects: company/reviews/ncm-batch1-final-qa-2026-10-14.md reports all 7 re-run at 34/34 pass, but at commit 33d7dfb. That commit is on session 2's unpushed branch and is not in this repository, so I cannot confirm the tested code is the code that shipped. Each Demo.tsx was changed again at 10:26-10:41. W-406 (qa-tester, re-file these records) is still `next`. Anomaly A2 below.

**Logging check, stale QA evidence.** For 221 of 635 published lessons, the newest QA record was committed before the newest Demo.tsx commit. For 60 of them, an artifacts/qa-* run passed on both viewports after that change, which leaves **161 with no on-disk evidence that the current code passes**. Two cautions. Commit time is not run time, and artifacts/ is not committed, so this is an upper bound on missing evidence, not a count of broken lessons. Most of those edits are probably copy fixes. This is W-668 (evaluation-steward) seen from the published side.

Anything that looks interesting is probably wrong (Twyman). Before explaining a move, check logging, sample ratios and novelty.

## 2b. Agents (from `npm run metrics -- --md`, "Agents" table)

**Logging check first: the event log was backfilled today and now runs to 2026-10-15 09:02.** 811 events are dated after yesterday's 15:20 cut-off. They include 125 `usage` records (17.4M tokens) and 121 dispatches, but **0 `stopped` events**, because the backfill read finished runs from the transcript. **company/ops/ledger.jsonl was not backfilled**: its last line is still 2026-10-14 15:20 (61.2M). So `node tools/ledger.mjs report`'s "96k per published lesson" divides yesterday's tokens by today's lessons. Do not quote it.

**New finding: resumed runs are counted more than once.** Twenty-six agent labels have more than one `usage` record, and the repeats are near-identical and rising. Tokens and minutes are cumulative, for example "Release manager: publish 79" at 53k/8 min, 54k/33 min, 55k/38 min, and "Build wave J: life" at 229k twice. Summing them, as `metrics` does, counts the same run again: **4.3M of 78.6M (5.5%)**, of which 2.0M is in the backfilled window. Medium-high confidence in the direction. Exactly how much is double-counted depends on what the harness's `subagent_tokens` means on resume (the per-run total so far, or something else), and I have not confirmed that. Anomaly A1.

- **Tokens per published lesson: 101k -> 122k is mostly not a cost increase.** The 101k divided tokens to 15:20 by lessons counted later. Matching the periods moves it only to 104k, so the period mismatch is a small part of the jump. The bigger part is that it is a cumulative ratio. After 15:20 the numerator grew 28% (+17.4M) and the denominator 8% (587 -> 635). Most of that spend went to work that publishes nothing yet: History drafts 1.45M, NCM, Big Ideas, Books and Life Hacks engines, review-publish 2.39M, and project reviews. Charging those 17.4M to the 48 lessons r6 published gives about 360k each, which is equally misleading. **Quote cost per lesson as a range with its period: 100-117k de-duplicated, as of 2026-10-15 09:02.** That needs a cohort cost (tokens per lesson by slug) before it is used for budgeting. Anomaly A1.
- **Rework 48% (up 3 points): aging and exposure, not a worse upstream.** The definition is version > 1. Since yesterday, 34 more lessons count as revised and 15 lessons are new. I did not snapshot yesterday's per-lesson versions, so I cannot say which cohort the 34 come from. Split by exposure: **58% (431/743) of lessons with a learner review have been revised, against 12% (25/217) without one.** By build day: 74% for lessons built 10-12, 48% for 10-13 and 41% for 10-14. Published lessons are at 57%, because publishing needs review and fixes. Life Hacks (200 lessons, 33 revised, mostly unreviewed) pulls the total down. Without it, rework is 56%. Rework will keep rising as lessons age, whatever the brief quality. A rise only says the upstream got worse if rework rises **within the same age band** and the causes in build.md point at the brief. Anomaly A3.
- **EXP-003, opus 52% vs sonnet 67%: the gap fits a time-and-mix confound, not a model effect, and the "harder lessons went to opus" story is not what the data shows.**
  - All 82 sonnet lessons were added on 2026-10-13. Opus lessons are spread over 10-12 (35/107, 33%), 10-13 (199/319, 62%) and 10-14 (90/193, 47%, including Life Hacks at 0/14).
  - **Same day: sonnet 67% vs opus 62%, +4.7 points ± 11.5 (95%). Same day and same domain (Mantel-Haenszel): +4.1 points.** Both are consistent with no difference.
  - The pooled +14.7 points comes from opus also owning the early pre-earn-the-reveal lessons and the Life Hacks first reviews.
  - On the selection worry, sonnet lessons carry slightly *more* claims than same-day opus lessons (5.5 vs 5.1 per lesson). Claim count is a crude difficulty proxy, but it does not support "harder lessons went to opus". Lessons with new interaction types were not coded, so selection on difficulty is unmeasured, not excluded.
  - Attribution is still a text match ("sonnet build" in build.md; everything else counts as opus). The registered design had 20 sonnet lessons (economics w5, chemistry w5) against the same-day opus waves, but the metric counts 82 against all opus.
  - **The committed analysis is the same-day comparison, and it does not fire the falsifier (more than 15 points below opus).** It also gives no evidence that sonnet is better. The token arm stands as recorded in EXP-003 (60-70% of opus, at the edge of the <= 60% prediction). Anomaly A4.
- **Roles never dispatched: 45 of 96.** The backfill fixed two false positives from yesterday (analytics-steward and domain-scout now show runs).
  - **Attribution gap:** cm-history is listed as never dispatched, yet company/domains/briefs/history.md says cm-history re-checked and extended the briefs (W-742). Either that work ran under another label or the chief of staff's office did it. Ten History build notes say the brief gave no title or hook, which is the check a category manager does.
  - **Checks being skipped (dispatch them, don't retire them):** privacy-reviewer has 3 open items (W-086, W-892, W-932) while `/api/events` is in production; learning-designer, while builders still write their own recall questions.
  - qa-tester has 9 runs against 635 published lessons and W-406 still open (see section 2).
  - The strand-level category managers and the dormant localization, R&D and personalization roles are the same as yesterday. Retiring them is an org decision for chief-of-staff / head-of-product, not mine.
- **Stop rate: 4%, but the overloaded window is still unmeasured.** The backfill carries 121 dispatches after 15:20 and zero stops, because it read finished runs only. The 4% therefore cannot show whether yesterday's 20-agent peak broke the 10% line. Yesterday's evidence of host load (69 s QA at 17 UTC, raised timeouts) still stands. Wave J build runs ran 137-188 min, against a demo-builder median of 22.
- **Tokens per run by role, against yesterday:** demo-builder 149k -> 156k, learner-evaluator 179k -> 181k, fact-checker 131k -> 135k, general-purpose 177k -> 182k. The backfilled demo-builder runs average 198k (31 records), but 7 of those 31 are repeat records of resumed runs (A1). The rest are Wave J and pilot builds that ran 2-3 h on an overloaded host. I see no evidence of a bloated brief. The cleaner test is build tokens per lesson for Wave J (about 45 lessons, not yet in company/ops/waves.json) against w3b+w4's 21k.
